items.streamTitle: New mediation estimators separated individual and peer pathways under interference
items.streamSummary: A semiparametric framework decomposes intervention mediation into own-person and peer-spillover components despite treatment-induced confounding. Mathematical and simulation results do not establish validity in untested influence studies.
items.attribution: Ham, Cheng and Li — arXiv preprint (causal mediation methods, November 9)

items.streamTitle: EU investigators described opportunistic foreign amplification of French unrest
items.streamSummary: Reuters reported EU and French assessments of foreign-aligned accounts exploiting French unrest with fabricated narratives. Investigators found no evidence these actors caused the protests; engagement figures do not establish persuasion.
items.attribution: Reuters — November 9 original reporting on internal EU and French government assessments

items.streamTitle: Synthetic populations lost temporal validity despite sophisticated generation methods
items.streamSummary: Multi-year evaluations found synthetic agent populations lose representativeness; ideal future-informed static projection worked best but was impractical, while aggregate-based updates failed to preserve some attribute dependencies.
items.attribution: Darsel, Côme, Rich, Pereira and Oukhellou — arXiv preprint (synthetic-population forecasting comparison)

items.streamTitle: WorkflowArena tested whether AI agents can design and execute useful team structures
items.streamSummary: WorkflowArena scored 145 integrated professional tasks across nine models and found domain-dependent orchestration behavior; workflow design sometimes improved fixed weaker executors. Real research validity was not established.
items.attribution: Jiang et al. — arXiv preprint, WorkflowArena (verified multi-agent workflow benchmark)

items.streamTitle: EU launched a pilot public repository of political-ad provenance and targeting disclosures
items.streamSummary: The European Commission opened a voluntary pilot repository for political-ad disclosure on October 12. It enables structured sponsor and targeting records in principle but is not yet evidence of full coverage, enforcement or behavioral effects.
items.attribution: European Commission, Directorate-General for Communication — official pilot infrastructure announcement (October 12)

items.streamTitle: A new commentary treats AI slop as a community judgment, not merely a detection label
items.streamSummary: A November 9 Nature Human Behaviour Comment reframes AI slop as context-dependent unwanted content judged by communities, not synonymous with AI origin. It is conceptual, not an evaluated moderation intervention.
items.attribution: So et al. — Nature Human Behaviour (Comment)

items.streamTitle: Culture shapes episodic remembering across personal, legal and political contexts
items.streamSummary: A November 9 Nature Reviews Psychology review argues that culture shapes episodic remembering and interpersonal reconstruction, with legal and political applications. It synthesizes prior evidence; it is not a new causal experiment.
items.attribution: Wang, Jobson, Mert and Vredeveldt — Nature Reviews Psychology (research review)

items.streamTitle: Synthetic advertising personas performed better with fewer demographic details
items.streamSummary: A November 6 preprint benchmarked simulated ad audiences against campaign records across five demographic segments. Leaner persona signals produced lower prediction error than richer prompts; validation outside the campaign remains open.
items.attribution: Choi, Lee, Seo, Lee and Choi — arXiv preprint (real-campaign synthetic-persona benchmark)

items.streamTitle: An LLM simulation replication changed dramatically after one overlooked instruction
items.streamSummary: ODD+LLM shows that one missed role instruction materially changed naming-game convergence, while a review of 28 studies found pervasive missing implementation details. It is a reproducibility advance, not human validation.
items.attribution: Downes, Milletich and Hirst — arXiv preprint (ODD+LLM reporting method and replication study)

items.streamTitle: Randomized agent interventions enabled estimation of when human review helps
items.streamSummary: A November 6 preprint estimates dynamic causal effects of randomized verification and steering within AI-agent trajectories; results vary by action and state. Benefits in deployed research workflows remain untested.
items.attribution: Sawarni, Xing, Zrnic, Johari and Syrgkanis — arXiv preprint (causal agent-evaluation framework)

items.streamTitle: Deciding before seeing AI advice improved performance in a 130-person experiment
items.streamSummary: A November 6 preprint reports that a human-first AI advice sequence improved decisions in a 130-person experiment versus concurrent or absent assistance. Mechanisms and operational generalization remain untested.
items.attribution: Keke, Eisenhardt and Meske — arXiv preprint (human–AI decision experiment)

items.streamTitle: Composable causal benchmarks isolated missingness and misleading variance shortcuts
items.streamSummary: A November 6 causal-methods preprint introduced configurable time-series benchmarks with paired counterfactuals; 81 discovery and 18 effect-estimation configurations exposed missingness and variance-related failure modes.
items.attribution: Ferdous and Gani — arXiv preprint (DTCD causal benchmark toolkit)

items.streamTitle: Ukraine messaging study measured coherence without claiming persuasion effects
items.streamSummary: A November 2 NATO StratCom COE report applied AI-enabled coding to Ukraine's May–November 2023 official and aligned messaging. It measures cross-platform narrative coherence, not accuracy or persuasive effectiveness.
items.attribution: Fredheim, Heap and Catena — NATO StratCom Centre of Excellence (40-page empirical report)

items.streamTitle: VR workload study found cognitive dual-task demands outweighed visual and audio clutter
items.streamSummary: A 24-person immersive shopping study found a secondary arithmetic task imposed more mental workload than moving visual characters or ambient noise. Physiological differences varied across people; operational transfer is untested.
items.attribution: Cucinella et al. — Applied Ergonomics (within-participant VR experiment; online May, November issue)

items.streamTitle: New peer-reviewed evidence finds AI agents amplify modeled social contagion
items.streamSummary: A November 6 npj Complexity study compared AI and human adoption thresholds in two choice paradigms and found lower thresholds in five LLM-based agents; modeled mixed networks spread behavior further, without real-world network validation.
items.attribution: Feng, Hitz, Lazzaro et al. — npj Complexity (human-comparison experiments and diffusion simulations)

items.streamTitle: Spatial audio guided anticipatory gaze and reduced collisions in VR navigation
items.streamSummary: A Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience VR eye-tracking experiment found that spatial auditory cues directed gaze ahead of visual events; removing sound delayed orienting and increased collisions. Field-training transfer is untested.
items.attribution: Kondyli and Leszczyński — Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience (VR/eye-tracking experiment)

items.streamTitle: Election fact-checks faced severe coverage, timing and audience-reach constraints
items.streamSummary: An analysis of 2022 US midterm misinformation on X found just 48% of 135 prominent narratives fact-checked, a four-day median delay, and correction links near 1% of conversation posts; effects on beliefs were not measured.
items.attribution: Wack, Duskin and Hodel — Political Communication (observational election-information analysis)

items.streamTitle: Five profiles separated entrepreneurial goals from intended implementation
items.streamSummary: A 934-student Chinese survey identified five entrepreneurial goal–implementation profiles; psychological and social capital correlated with their membership. Self-reported implementation is not observed action.
items.attribution: Hao and Hou — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (latent-profile survey)

items.streamTitle: Formal crisis support was not always experienced as meaningful support
items.streamSummary: In a 290-staff UK university survey, formal crisis-support resources differed from experienced support; leadership communication and accessibility shaped reported perceptions. Qualitative findings are not causal tests.
items.attribution: Kassem and Mitsakis — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (qualitative-dominant staff survey)

items.streamTitle: Independent assessment found accelerated AI benchmarks but uncertain R&D attribution
items.streamSummary: METR estimated Anthropic's measured AI capability improvements accelerated about 1.9× since late 2025, but attribution to AI-assisted R&D is uncertain and supporting evidence was partly withheld.
items.attribution: METR — Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic (November 5 report)

items.streamTitle: RAND proposed multi-factor assessment of Air Force squadron leadership
items.streamSummary: A RAND Air Force study synthesized leadership competencies and derailers and outlined a multi-method, potentially AI-supported five-year selection pilot; no operational selection benefit was demonstrated.
items.attribution: Evans et al. — RAND Project AIR FORCE, RR-A4215-1 (research report)

items.streamTitle: RAND found allied responses to US drawdown depend on how it is signaled
items.streamSummary: RAND's October 28 scenario analysis suggests allied defense responses hinge on the process and credibility of US retrenchment, with coordination and suddenness affecting predicted trust. These are forecasts, not observed effects.
items.attribution: Priebe et al. — RAND, RR-A5006-1 (peer-reviewed prepublication scenario analysis)

items.streamTitle: Closed-loop VR cues restored task alignment faster than fixed reminders
items.streamSummary: In a 48-person VR study, gaze/head-signal-triggered cues reduced median task realignment time from 10.8 to 6.2 seconds versus periodic cues, with lower reported disruption. Operational transfer is untested.
items.attribution: Kim and Lee — IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics, ReAlign (within-subjects XR evaluation)

items.streamTitle: Research agents produced plausible papers but failed all 135 open-problem rubrics
items.streamSummary: In a DOE-scientist-defined benchmark, none of 135 AI-agent follow-up papers met all research requirements and 114 failed integrity checks. Reproducible logs and requirement-by-requirement evaluation are critical.
items.attribution: Kim et al. — arXiv preprint, Into the Unknown (open scientific-agent benchmark)
